Triage (maintainer-authorized one-off pass, 2026-08-09, registered on objectstack#6015): **promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`.** An ADR whose Consequences section contradicts its own P2/P4 rulings misleads every reader who stops at the summary — and this ADR governs where permission facets get authored, a question agents act on. Deliverable: reconcile the Consequences bullet to the P2/P4 direction (the later, specific rulings win over the earlier summary sentence), one docs-only PR. ⚠️ `docs/adr/**` edit: **maintainer-merged only**, per standing discipline.

## ⛔ GOVERNED SURFACE — this PR must NOT reach the merge queue

`docs/adr/**` is a governed path. The standing discipline, restated by triage on this very card (*"⚠️ `docs/adr/**` edit: maintainer-merged only"*):

- Open the PR as **draft** and **leave it draft**. ⛔ Never mark ready, ⛔ never enqueue, ⛔ never enable auto-merge.
- Human merge **is** the review record. There is no machine that will stop you; this instruction is the only gate.
- I will request review from / assign `os-zhuang` and list it under "awaiting a human merge" in the round report.

Everything else about the PR is normal: `Fixes #3794`, a changeset if the presence gate asks for one (`node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — an **empty frontmatter** changeset is this repo's declared "releases nothing" form, and is the right answer for a docs-only diff).

## Adjudication (triage, 2026-08-09) — direction is settled

> reconcile the Consequences bullet to the P2/P4 direction (**the later, specific rulings win over the earlier summary sentence**), one docs-only PR.

So: the **Consequences** bullet is the wrong text, and P2/P4 are right. ⛔ Do not "fix" P2/P4 to match Consequences, and ⛔ do not treat this as an open design question — the code already sits on the P2/P4 side, which the card measured:

- `sys_capability` multi-select is rendered by Studio's `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`.
- Setup's six facets all go through a read-only `permission-facet-link` summary + deep link.

The card's own suggested replacement is a reasonable starting point, not a mandate:

> Capabilities are designed once, in Studio, through the `sys_capability` picker; Setup only assigns permission sets to users.

## The second half of the deliverable — and the part most likely to be skipped

The card asks for more than the one sentence, and triage kept it:

> 顺带核一遍 Consequences 其余各条与 P1–P4 的实现是否同步。

`#3308` already proved this ADR's phased landing left one stale residue behind (the `capability-multiselect` widget name), which is evidence the file has more than one. **Read every Consequences bullet against P1–P4 and against the code, and report what you checked** — including the bullets you found already correct. A finding of "the other five are accurate, here is how I verified each" is a complete delivery; silently fixing only the one sentence the card names is not.

If you find a second contradiction whose correct direction is genuinely unclear, ⛔ do not guess — leave that bullet, and report it as an open question. An ADR is exactly the place where a confident wrong sentence does the damage this card is about.

⛔ **Verify before you write**: this ADR is 16 days past the card's measurement. Confirm the contradictory sentence is still there, with a control probe (something you know is present) so a zero-hit reads as real. If it has already been fixed, that is a with-evidence close, not a diff to manufacture.

## ACCEPT — PR #5970 (R35, `domain:ui`)

Reviewed against GitHub and against `origin/main`, not against the report's self-description.

**Checklist:** draft ✅ · base `main` ✅ · `Fixes #3794` first line ✅ · 1 file, +12/−6, prose only ✅ · fence honoured (nothing outside `docs/adr/0056-permission-editing-studio.md`) ✅ · `mergeable_state: clean` ✅ · no changeset, on the presence gate's own verdict ✅. The `documentation` label came from the repo labeler bot, not the agent.

### Spot-checks I ran myself, because hunk 2 is dev-initiated scope

Hunk 1 is the sentence the card names, and it is a direct application of the settled direction. **Hunk 2 is the dev's own find**, so I verified its four load-bearing citations against `origin/main` rather than accepting them:

| claim | verified |
|---|---|
| Decision 3 says "No exception for `system_permissions`" | ✅ line **169** |
| Decision 1 says "the same component, two entry points" | ✅ line **162**, with Setup's `setup.access` env-scope route at **161** |
| the bootstrap concern is resolved by an entry point **inside Setup** | ✅ lines **171–173** |
| A2 revised — the bootstrap knot "doesn't arise" | ✅ lines **51–56** |

And the reading that settles it, which neither the card nor triage cited — **the ADR's own Status line, line 3**:

> Revised from the original **Option B** (which kept `system_permissions` editable in Setup as an exception) to the **pure model** below: Studio designs *every* facet, Setup only assigns + shows read-only summaries.

So both edited bullets were Option-B residue in a document whose Status line already records Option B as superseded. The old bullet 5 (*"hence P2 keeps that grant in Setup"*) did not merely sit oddly beside Decision 3 — it asserted the exception Decision 3 refuses **by name**. Finding it was in scope (triage kept the "核一遍其余各条" half), the fix is grounded in four statements already in the file, and keeping it as a **separate self-contained hunk** so a reviewer can drop it alone is the right shape for a governed surface.

The audit reported its negative results too — bullets 2, 3, 4a verified accurate with code citations (`PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx:980`, `applyFieldWidgetOverrides` at `data-objectstack/src/index.ts:3361/3397-3402`, and all three Setup surfaces short-circuiting read-only). Reporting what was checked and found *correct* is what makes the audit half a real deliverable rather than a claim.

### Your two open questions — PM ruling

**4b (`RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema` / `AdminScopeSchema` "read … from `@objectstack/spec`") — option A, leave as written.** Your measurement is right (imported nowhere; only a comment at `clientValidation.ts:526`, with local mirror interfaces in `PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx`), but the bullet's own trailing clause *"the editors couple to those shapes"* is its gloss on "read", so this is a **wording** question, not a **direction** contradiction — and the ruled axis here is Consequences-vs-P1–P4 direction. Not worth a rework round. ✅ Declining to guess at wording where only the facts, not the direction, were in question was the right call, and putting the sharpened alternative in the PR body means the maintainer can take it with one line in the review this path requires anyway.

**4c (Q7 env-scope projection) — option A, leave as written.** Self-labelled an open *framework* follow-up, nothing in this repo can confirm or falsify it, and it is not a Consequences↔P1–P4 mismatch. Outside the fence. Correctly left.

### ⛔ Landing: this PR does NOT enqueue

`docs/adr/**` is a governed path. Per standing discipline and triage's note on this card, human merge **is** the review record:

- Staying **draft**. ⛔ Not marked ready, ⛔ not enqueued, ⛔ no auto-merge.
- Review requested from `os-zhuang`.
- Listed under "awaiting a human merge" in the R35 round report.

CI not yet read — the PR's checks started 10:06Z and this seat's rule is to read gates **by name, once, ~11 minutes after** the run's own `started_at`. Reading early is a discipline failure; the reading will be taken and posted on the PR. It does not gate this ACCEPT, since nothing here reaches the merge queue either way.
